JSR check_for_mover_collision_with_movers\ grind (mmr3a): cchm_with_a_g1's first two instructions in line: no collision (the hot case)
    BCC mmr_clear_g3a               \ is not hostile (C = 0), and goes straight on without the JSR/RTS pair and the BCS
    JSR mmr_hostile_g3a             \ Returns carry set if hostile collision occurred (A, X = the screen address, as cchm_with_a_g1 left them)
    BCS skip_changing_screen_address_23e5
.mmr_clear_g3a

    LDA mover_screen_address_low
    LDY x_delta
    DEY
    BMI skip_changing_screen_address_23e5
    JSR add_delta_to_screen_address_in_AX
.skip_changing_screen_address_23e5
    STA mover_screen_address_low

    JSR check_for_mover_collision_with_movers\ Returns carry set if collision, X = mover collided with
    BCC not_hostile                 \ grind: no collision is not hostile (C = 0); both callers reload Y
.mmr_hostile_g3a                   \ grind (mmr3a): move_mover_right's JSR for a collision (C = 1 here)
    JSR check_for_hostile_collision \ Returns carry set if collision was hostile
candidates.summary: move_mover_right: check_for_mover_collision_with_movers called in line, and the no-collision case (the only one in 1,500 passes) falls straight to the screen-address reload, instead of JSR cchm_with_a_g1 / BCC / LDX / LDA / RTS / BCS. The hostile check is reached by a JSR to a new label inside cchm_with_a_g1 (mmr_hostile_g3a). Saves JSR 6 + RTS 6 + BCS 2 = 14 cycles a call, grows the code by 9 bytes, which moves page crossings (see relies_on). ALTERNATIVE to the check_for_hostile_collision candidate (overlapping on purpose: the two together slide the code 11 bytes and cost more in page crossings than they gain).
candidates.equivalence: Entry: move_mover_right reaches the JSR with A = new x low, Y = new x high, as it did for cchm_with_a_g1 (which began with the same JSR, no TXA). No collision (C = 0): cchm went BCC not_hostile, LDX $C3, LDA $C2, RTS with C = 0, then BCS not taken; now BCC mmr_clear_g3a does the same LDX, LDA with the same A, X, C = 0. Collision (C = 1): JSR mmr_hostile_g3a runs exactly the rest of cchm_with_a_g1 (JSR check_for_hostile_collision, BCC not_hostile, DEC/LDA/STA/LDA/STA/STZ when hostile, LDX/LDA/RTS) and returns C = 1 if hostile (DEC zp, LDA, STA, STZ, LDX leave C alone) and C = 0 otherwise; BCS skip then does what the original BCS did with A, X the screen address; a non-hostile collision falls into mmr_clear_g3a and reloads the same A, X (harmless). Y, N, Z, V are dead at both points (LDY x_delta follows). Stack: one level less on the hot path, same depth on the hostile path. move_mover_left still enters through check_for_collision_after_horizontal_move / cchm_with_a_g1, unchanged (label kept, tail unchanged). Nothing else refers to cchm_with_a_g1 or enters it +n (grepped src/ and tools/).
candidates.relies_on: Page crossings: adds 9 bytes after move_mover_right, so everything in game.6502 up to the SKIP before &3400 moves up 9 (the SKIP shrinks; 193 bytes free in the shipping build). Re-evaluated every branch in build/strykers-debug_lives.lst for a +9 slide with the measured profile: new crossings 27F6 BCC search_prefilter_next (about 7,800 taken in 1,500 passes, about +5 cycles a pass), 23ED BRA um_populate (+1 a pass), 22EC and 26F4 (negligible); crossings that go away 28F5, 28F9, 2AF8 (about -0.8 a pass); 21FB and 27EF become crossing but are almost never taken. Net expected loss from crossings about 5 cycles a pass against 15 gained. Indexed reads: um_next and keys are ASSERTed not to cross, the others are small tables far from a page end. ASSERT HI(move_mover_up_and_right) = HI(move_mover_down_and_left) still holds (&20D0/&20E2). Any slide of 8 or more bytes costs on 27F6, so do not stack this with the other candidate (+11).

candidates.summary: check_for_hostile_collision: the carry-clear exit (no collision; 1.77 times a pass from move_mover_up/down's JSR) takes the BCC before loading the type, skipping a 4-cycle LDA movers_type_and_colour,X whose A is dead there; the load moves after the BCC and a CPY #0 restores the Z the player test needs. Saves 4 cycles on the no-collision exit, costs 2 on the rare collision path, grows by 2 bytes. The old text spans move_mover_right and cchm_with_a_g1 unchanged (only the last four lines change) on purpose, so it overlaps (is an alternative to) the in-line cchm candidate: stacked they slide the code 11 bytes. Take this one if that one fails the gate.
candidates.equivalence: Only the order of LDA type,X and BCC changes. Callers: check_for_collision_after_vertical_move (BCS vertical_collision_b245f, else no_collision: LDX/LDA through Y = mover_to_update, which overwrite A) and cchm_with_a_g1 (BCC not_hostile; C = 1 there always; LDX/LDA overwrite A). Nothing enters check_for_hostile_collision + n (grepped). On the carry-clear exit by BCC: Y = mover_to_update was loaded before the branch as before; A is no longer the type and no caller reads it. The other carry-clear exit (is_player_2411's CMP #&0F BCC) still has A = type. With C = 1 the path is LDY, BCC not taken, LDA type,X (same byte, X untouched), CPY #0, BNE: Z is the Y = 0 test exactly as the LDY set it. CPY #0 sets C = 1 (Y >= 0); the paths after read C only after their own CMP/CPY (CPY #&0C, CMP #&0F) so nothing sees the change, and the exits set C themselves (SEC / CLC). N and V dead. Hostile paths are the same 2 cycles slower.
